GOAL: orient in the frozen repo and issue126 artifacts before proposing.
READ: workspace listing, results/research/issue126.
OPEN: what the hard prefix score Q_H is and what proxy exists.

GOAL: choose a coupling position not covered by earlier rounds.
READ: the round history in the prompt (BRANCHCURV-SID, GEO-SHELL-RQ, GEOPFX-SID, GEO_REPAIR, GYRO-TARGET-RQ, KAPPA_BRANCH, LORENTZ_CONE_RQ, SUCC-TAN-RQ, behaviour_anchored_geodesic_charts, cocond-markov-poincare-ot, CURVCELL-SID, SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ, poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, SUCC-GEO-CBTAB). No filesystem read tool exists in this Code Mode catalog, so the repo itself could not be inspected; the design therefore relies on the round history and on the issue126 summary given in the prompt.
OBSERVED: every earlier proposal puts behaviour into a per-item WEIGHT (successor mass, transition mass, Fréchet weighting, Sinkhorn cost, cone/tangent transport) or adds a prefix-rank proxy loss. None uses a measured behaviour statistic as the STATE VARIABLE of the curvature itself. Also, no earlier proposal varies curvature per RQ level from a measured quantity.
REASONING: the differentiated move is a closed feedback loop: the hard prefix score Q_l (the Q_H of issue126, per level) is not optimised as a proxy but is fed back as the curvature of the level-l quantizer metric. Behaviour enters only through the scalar curvature, geometry enters only as d_c/exp_c, so both are individually necessary and the path is a single one. Constants are derived from two measured quantities (Q_l, mean latent norm rho_l), so no sweep is needed.
OPEN: write the full proposal block.

FINAL ANSWER (compact; full block is in the assistant response):
IDEA: CURVCTRL-SID
TITLE: Per-level RQ curvature is driven by the measured hard prefix-transition hit rate of that level.
MOTIVATION: level-1 code must predict level-2 or the generator prefix is a coin flip; issue126's Q_H ranks recall but was only a diagnostic.
NOVELTY: no loss term, no per-item behaviour weight; Q_l is a per-level state variable setting curvature; curvature varies across RQ levels; answers issue126 by feeding the hard score back instead of optimising its proxy.
CHANGE: every 5 epochs measure Q_l (fraction of training transitions whose endpoints share the level-l prefix) and rho_l (mean latent norm); derive c_l; use Poincare distance of curvature -c_l in the level-l assignment and commitment.
SPECIFICATION: E = frozen hash-subsample (<=2^20) of training consecutive-item directed transitions. Q_l = mean 1[p_l(i)=p_l(j)], clip [1e-3,1]. c_l=(1/Q_l-1)/(rho_l^2+1e-8), cap 0.99/max||z_l||^2, floor 1e-4, smoothed by 1/min(t+1,10) and clamped to factor 2. exp_0^c(z)=tanh(sqrt(c)||z||)/(sqrt(c)||z||)z; d_c(u,v)=(2/sqrt(c))artanh(sqrt(c)||(-u)(+)v||). Assignment k*=argmin_k d_{c_l}(exp(z_l),exp(e_k)); residual and codebook update stay Euclidean; L_commit=0.25 d^2.
COST: no new params; +1.89e7 curved distances/forward (5.7e7 with backward) = +8..20 ms/step, +10..24 min per card over 72000 steps; statistic pass 600x5 ms <5 s.
HYPOTHESIS: Q_l rises over Stage 2 (flat when behaviour off), c_l grows with depth, Stage3 test_recall@10 > 0.065.
RISKS: Q_l near constant -> fixed curvature; feedback oscillation; artanh saturation; single-run seed noise.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: hard per-level training prefix-transition hit rate Q_l plus rho_l.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: training split only, consecutive in-session pairs, fixed hashed edge sample, applied to current hard SID table every 5 epochs, stop-grad.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: no val/test interactions ever loaded; only aggregate training counts; scalars are global per level, cannot memorise an eval item.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare ball, curvature -c_l (c_l derived, not learned), origin exp map, Mobius addition, Poincare distance.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: inside the RQ quantizer level-l nearest-code assignment and level-l commitment term.
COUPLING PATH: transitions -> prefixes -> Q_l,rho_l -> c_l -> d_{c_l} -> code index + commitment -> gradients -> new prefixes -> next Q_l.
COUPLING EQUATION: c_l=(1/Q_l-1)/(rho_l^2+1e-8); k*=argmin_k (2/sqrt(c_l))artanh(sqrt(c_l)||(-exp(z_l))(+)(exp(e_k))||).
OBSERVABLES: Q_l trace, c_l trace, prefix hit rate under issue126 harness, code-usage entropy, distinct level-2 children per level-1 code, Stage3 test_recall@10.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: Q_l pinned so c_l=1.0 all levels (unit-curvature geometry, no feedback).
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: c_l=0, exp=id, squared Euclidean, Q_l still logged.
ABLATION BOTH ON: derived c_l active; the only arm trained this round.
SPEC EQUATIONS: as in SPECIFICATION; loss = L_recon+L_commit+L_codebook unchanged otherwise.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: in: frozen training edge sample, hard SID table, level-l latents and K code vectors; out: L scalars plus per-batch code indices and curved commitment.
SAFEGUARDS: float64 stats, artanh clip 1-1e-7, c_l cap 0.99/max||z||^2, factor-2 clamp, harmonic smoothing, Q_l clip, degenerate-collapse mode is the Euclidean baseline (NaN-free).
END IDEA

STAGE: design-space selection for the second (extra) idea.

GOAL: pick one coupling position not covered by the earlier round names (BRANCHCURV-SID, GEO-SHELL-RQ, GEOPFX-SID, GEO_REPAIR, GYRO-TARGET-RQ, KAPPA_BRANCH, LORENTZ_CONE_RQ, SUCC-TAN-RQ, behaviour_anchored_geodesic_charts, CURVCELL-SID, SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ, cocond-markov-poincare-ot, BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, SUCC-GEO-CBTAB, poincare-frechet-successor-codebook) and not a re-run of the issue126 prefix-rank proxy.

READ: the task brief, the earlier-round list, and the issue126 finding (Q_H ranks with test R@10; open question whether the proxy is optimisable). No repository files were readable from this session (catalog exposes browser/opencode/progress only), so the novelty claim is made against the named mechanisms, not against unseen code.

OBSERVED: the taken positions are behaviour-weighted assignment/OT, successor-Fréchet codebook updates, tangent residuals, curvature learning, prefix ranking, behaviour-anchored charts, shell/allocation variants. The untouched position is the QUANTIZER'S TRAINING DISTRIBUTION: which points the RQ-VAE is asked to reconstruct.

REASONING: choose a behaviour-conditioned Poincare geodesic midpoint as an extra reconstruction target. Behaviour picks the pair from training-only co-consumption; curvature defines the path; the midpoint bows toward the ball origin, i.e. toward the generic region that the level-1 token covers. Removing behaviour removes the pair; removing curvature changes the point. This is one connected pathway ending in the SID, needs no new parameters, no tuning (midpoint alpha=1/2 is canonical; ball radius 0.9 is a documented safety constant; radial scale is measured max train norm), and costs about 2x Stage-2 compute with zero inference cost.

OPEN: whether extra between-item targets actually pull real items' coarse prefixes together rather than creating a dedicated virtual-point code; that is exactly what the single run and the recorded diagnostics decide. Recorded answer follows.

GOAL: choose a coupling position not among the named earlier mechanisms and not a rerun of the issue126 prefix proxy.
READ: brief, earlier-round names, issue126 note (Q_H tracks test R@10). No repo files readable in this session (catalog has browser/opencode/progress only).

REASONING: untouched position = the quantizer's TRAINING DISTRIBUTION. Pick a training-only co-consumption pair, build the c=-1 Poincare geodesic midpoint, add it as an extra reconstruction target. Behaviour selects the pair; curvature defines a midpoint that bows toward the ball origin (generic coarse region); either removal changes the target, gradient and SID. No new parameters; midpoint alpha=1/2 canonical; 0.9 ball radius and measured M are derived/documented, not tuned.
OPEN: extra targets may create a dedicated virtual code instead of pulling real items together; the single run plus recorded diagnostics decides. Full answer follows.

GOAL: choose a coupling position not among the named earlier mechanisms and not a rerun of the issue126 prefix proxy.
READ: brief, earlier-round names, issue126 note (Q_H tracks test R@10). No repo files readable here (catalog has browser/opencode/progress only).
OBSERVED: taken positions are behaviour-weighted assignment/OT, successor-Frechet codebook, tangent residuals, curvature learning, prefix ranking, shell allocation, behaviour-anchored charts.
REASONING: untouched position = the quantizer's TRAINING DISTRIBUTION. Pick a training-only co-consumption pair, build the c=-1 Poincare geodesic midpoint, add it as an extra reconstruction target. Behaviour selects the pair; curvature makes the midpoint bow toward the ball origin (generic coarse region); either removal changes the target, gradient and SID. No new parameters; alpha=1/2 canonical; R=0.9 and measured M are documented/derived.
OPEN: extra targets may create a dedicated virtual code instead of pulling real items together; the single run plus recorded diagnostics decides.

IDEA: GEO-MIX-PREFIX-RQ
TITLE: Geodesic-midpoint mixup gives co-consumed items a shared coarse Poincare prefix
MOTIVATION: Content-only SIDs give co-consumed items unrelated coarse prefixes, so the generator cannot use the history token to anticipate the successor.
NOVELTY: It changes no assignment, codebook, residual or prefix scorer. Unlike cocond-markov-poincare-ot, poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, SUCC-TAN-RQ, KAPPA_BRANCH and the issue126 proxy, it acts on the quantizer's TRAINING DISTRIBUTION: one curvature-defined virtual target at the exact geodesic midpoint.
CHANGE: From training-only co-consumption counts, add one virtual reconstruction target per connected item at the c=-1 Poincare geodesic midpoint of that item and a count-sampled neighbour; train the otherwise unchanged RQ-VAE on the 2N-point union.
SPECIFICATION: Build a row-normalised sparse co-consumption matrix P from train sessions (window 5). Map embeddings into the unit Poincare ball (R=0.9, M=max train norm). For each item with non-empty row sample j~P[i,:], set m_i=exp_{p_i}(0.5 log_{p_i}(p_j)), invert the chart, append as virtual target. Unchanged loss/encoder/codebook; SIDs inferred from real embeddings only.
COST: Preprocess: seconds (24556 midpoints, d~64). Train: 24 steps/epoch over 2N=49112 points, ~2046/step vs 1023, so ~2x encoder-decoder FLOPs/step and 1.6-2.0x Stage-2 wall clock over 3000 epochs. +~6.3 MB, no new params, no inference cost.
HYPOTHESIS: Origin-ward midpoints make level-1 cells behaviour-coherent: co-consumed pairs share first tokens more, successor first-token entropy falls, Stage3 test R@10 > 0.065. Only the hyperbolic midpoint bows toward the origin, so the Euclidean arm should lose this.
RISKS: A virtual-point code may appear without pulling real items together; smoothing may blur fine content; the graph is popularity-dominated; rare items may under-fit.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Windowed sequential co-consumption counts over training sessions.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: For each train session and ordered pair (u,v) with 1<=pos(v)-pos(u)<=5, C[u,v]+=1; A=C+C^T; A_ii=0; P[i,:]=A[i,:]/sum. One neighbour per item drawn once with the run seed, cached.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: Graph, M, midpoints and neighbours come from train sequences/embeddings only; val/test never read; SIDs from real embeddings.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Unit-curvature Poincare ball, c=-1, metric 4/(1-||x||^2)^2 I; Mobius addition, exp/log, geodesic midpoint.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Preprocessing and RQ-VAE reconstruction targets; it shapes the learned cells, not the assignment logits.
COUPLING PATH: graph -> pair -> geodesic -> curved midpoint -> virtual target -> reconstruction gradient -> level-1 codebook/encoder -> SID(i). No behaviour: no pair. Euclidean: different target. Either removal changes the computation.
COUPLING EQUATION: v_i=chart^{-1}(m_i), m_i=exp_{p_i}(0.5*log_{p_i}(p_{j(i)})), j(i)~P[i,:].
OBSERVABLES: mean level-1 centroid distance over co-consumed pairs (down); successor first-token entropy (down); fraction of first tokens changed; Stage3 test R@10. Diagnostics recorded, never gated.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: graph disabled, D'=D, same seed/epochs/RQ-VAE.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: same pairs and 2N set, m_i=(e_i+e_j)/2 raw, no ball maps.
ABLATION BOTH ON: full graph + c=-1 midpoint + 2N targets.
SPEC EQUATIONS: M=max||e_i||; p_i=0.9 e_i/M. x(+)y=((1+2<x,y>+||y||^2)x+(1-||x||^2)y)/(1+2<x,y>+||x||^2||y||^2). log_x(y)=2 artanh(||(-x)(+)y||)((-x)(+)y)/||(-x)(+)y||. exp_x(v)=x(+)(tanh(||v||/2)v/||v||). m_i=exp_{p_i}(0.5 log_{p_i}(p_j)); v_i=M m_i/0.9. Loss unchanged over real and virtual x.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: in: E (N x d), train sequences, W=5, R=0.9, c=-1, seed; out: X' (2N x d), row 2i=e_i, row 2i+1=v_i or e_i if no neighbour, plus index map.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp ||p||<=0.9-1e-6; denom max(.,1e-12); artanh arg min(.,1-1e-6); A_ii=0; skip zero-mass rows; handle ||e_i||=0; assert finite and ||v_i||<=max(||e_i||,||e_j||)+1e-6.
END IDEA
